scope: The candidate is a source-labelled evidence comparison spanning distinct preparations, not an assertion of a common product, interchangeable stereoisomers or catalog absence.
policy: Source-labelled preparation comparison with empty automatic match_aliases; preserve source_aliases separately. Do not assign generic/R/L catalog identities or current retail equivalence to all source preparations.
absence_limit: Withheld joins do not mean sulforaphane is absent from catalogs or unavailable.
conclusion: Retain source-specific actual-treatment functional research: aged-mouse performance, cardiac function and 12-week survival positives, plus an original-abstract-only diabetic grip positive. Preserve oral mdx nulls, histology and ex vivo colon responses separately. Exclude three withdrawn Sun sources from positive support. The preprint high-concentration PLK1/p-BubR1 result is mechanistic context only. No BUBR1 restoration, MVA benefit, common-product efficacy or superiority to provisional nominees is established.

additional_main_and_review_observations.oral_nulls: No detected oral contraction, resting-diameter, fecal-pellet-weight or cecal-mass improvement; no lean or tested-limb-muscle-mass benefit; CK/AST remain elevated.
additional_main_and_review_observations.non_null_additional_observations: Normalized weight gain and free-fluid percentage fell; diaphragm Tnfα transcript increased. Relative liver mass increased in both genotypes without an established toxicity diagnosis.
additional_main_and_review_observations.ex_vivo_design: Saline first, then 5 µM SFN; four 15-minute recordings in each period; resting diameter unchanged. Contraction counts are not force amplitude.
additional_main_and_review_observations.other_denominators: Initial n=20/genotype versus subsequent n=12/group plus n=8/group is unresolved. Figure 3 body-mass n=20/group, composition n=8, tissue weights n=10–12 and serum n=6–8 remain endpoint-specific.
additional_main_and_review_observations.separate_cultured_myotubes: 5–10 µM SFN raised Nrf2 protein/targets and reduced inflammatory transcripts in a separate main-text cell-culture description. The supplement was unreviewed; these are not oral target engagement or skeletal-strength results.
additional_main_and_review_observations.reading: Complete original main narrative and five captions through publisher PDF text/Europe PMC XML. No native pixels, supplement ZIP, raw observations or primer table. Independent review read the retained 27 body paragraphs and captions; no fresh retrieval.

citation.title: Sulforaphane prevents age-associated cardiac and muscular dysfunction through Nrf2 signaling

aging.decision: Retain a controlled actual-sulforaphane performance and cardiac research comparison with explicit dose, assay and cohort reporting limits. This source prevents a whole-compound negative verdict based only on other withdrawn/null studies, but establishes no clinical/MVA benefit or nominee superiority.

preparation.source_label: D,L-sulforaphane from Toronto Research Chemicals, North York, ON
preparation.vehicle: TD 96163 Teklad control diet or the same diet supplemented with SFN, ad libitum for 12 weeks

dose_conflict.interpretation: The original paper itself contains different denominators. Figure 5 explicitly describes a diet concentration. Do not repeat 442.5 mg/kg body weight as a resolved administered dose, silently substitute a diet denominator, or convert to mg/kg/day/HED.

design.species_strain: Male C57BL/6 mice; Discussion labels C57BL/B6J
design.allocation: Diet-controlled actual compound experiment; random allocation, concealment and blinded assessment are not reported in the reviewed Methods.
design.Methods_group_count: Four groups n=10/group; n=20/control groups and n=20/treated groups; experiment repeated with same number under similar conditions for certain experiments.
design.cohort_pooling_map: Not provided; do not independently credit a second replication or sum repeats into a claimed animal denominator.

outcomes.endpoint: Hanging/inverted-screen performance, described as grip strength
outcomes.anchor: Methods 2.4, Results SFN improves exercise capacity, Fig.2a caption
outcomes.comparison: Reported better old-SFN versus old-control performance; Figure 2 caption gives significant treatment thresholds P<.05 and P<.0001 across exercise/grip without separately reliable text-only assignment.
outcomes.critical_conflict: Methods remove mice at 60 seconds, yet treated group means are 64 and 86 seconds. The stated capped protocol cannot generate those means; no correction, uncapped/repeated-trial explanation or raw data is supplied.
outcomes.limit: Retain the reported direction with a material unresolved assay inconsistency. Do not call the reported difference a validated 47-second estimate, calibrated absolute-force gain, or direct muscle contractile measurement.

outcomes.reported_comparison: Old SFN diet better than old control; Discussion says approximately 1.5-fold exercise capacity.
outcomes.method: Acclimation; increasing speed/incline; exhaustion defined by inability to avoid repetitive shocks for 5 seconds. Time recorded, distance/work/power calculated.
outcomes.protocol_conflict: Methods alternate speed +2 m/min and incline +10% increments after 0% warm-up; Fig.2 caption describes 10% slope with increasing speed.
outcomes.limit: Whole-animal performance signal, not uniquely skeletal-muscle force. Heart effects, body/motivational factors and terminal-survivor selection remain relevant. No native graph digitization or unreported P assignment.

Small controlled observation during treatment, not a complete lifespan study. Death causes, formal exclusion flow and endpoint selection are unreported; terminal n=10 functional samples are not mapped to n=20 survival animals.

outcomes.anchor: Methods 2.5, Results/Fig.2c-d; Supplement S1–S8 cited but inaccessible
outcomes.procedure: EDL myofiber clusters from treated/control mice cultured for 72 h; images 0/48/72 h; marker-positive categories expressed as percentage of total immunostained cells on fibers and pooled across fibers.
outcomes.reported_result: Higher Pax7-positive and MyoD-positive progeny proportions in treated young/old groups; caption P<.001 with t test/two-way ANOVA.
outcomes.absolute_cell_count: Methods mention absolute satellite cells per fiber using DAPI after X-Gal, but highlighted results/figure caption report pooled percentages; no reliable absolute regenerative-output treatment estimate available here.
outcomes.limit: Activation/differentiation-associated phenotype, not demonstrated long-term self-renewal, preserved quiescent reserve, engraftment, serial-injury recovery or faithful chromosome segregation. Pooled-fiber unit and animal independence are unclear.

outcomes.test: ANOVA followed by Tukey; caption P<.001/P<.0001 thresholds
outcomes.cardiac_output: Reported improved in old mice; no significant treated-young cardiac-output difference.
outcomes.limit: Actual cardiac functional measurements; these can contribute to running performance, with no mediation separation or isolated skeletal-output attribution.

outcomes.heart: Reported significant improvement in old-mouse heart complex I, I+II and maximal respiration.
outcomes.skeletal_muscle: Similar treatment trends did not reach significance in skeletal muscle.
outcomes.limit: Do not promote abstract-level broad mitochondrial-restoration wording to a significant skeletal-muscle respiration treatment result. Duplicate tissue assays are not extra animals.

outcomes.assay: Nuclear Nrf2-ARE-binding ELISA and target-gene expression.
outcomes.reported: Main says binding rises in heart and skeletal muscle; Fig.6 caption specifies old heart n=5. qPCR tables use n=5 and source-described multiple-comparison tests.
outcomes.limit: Actual drug-associated pathway engagement. This study does not establish that Nrf2 is necessary or sufficient for its performance effects; genetic evidence in cited literature is not an SFN result.

statistics.general: Mean ± SD; unpaired Student t test for 2 groups; one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni/Tukey for >=3; logrank survival.
statistics.specific: Captions additionally refer to repeated-measures/two-way ANOVA. Table footnotes mix Tukey/two-way ANOVA and two-tailed t labels; printed four-star threshold P<.05 is internally inconsistent with usual figure notation and not repaired.

additional_reporting_limits: Methods fasting 10–12 h, Figure 1 text 8 h for fasting glucose and 4 h for IPGTT; no silent harmonization.
General treatment 12 weeks versus histology narrative after 2 months; supplementary images/timing not inspected.
Randomization/masking and how repeated experiments were pooled are not stated.
Native figure pixels and supplements were unavailable through the bounded ordinary routes; no reconstruction from imagined graphs.

safety.reported: No adverse effects observed; main reports unchanged body weight/food intake and hematological parameters, lower water intake, and fewer deaths in treated old mice.
safety.limits: Hematology Table S1 inaccessible and not independently read. No systematic full adverse-event/organ/pathology program or pediatric/cancer-context safety claim. Dose and exposure ambiguity prevents a clinical regimen or safety-margin inference.

aging.retraction_boundary: The introduction cites Sun2015 dystrophic-muscle work. Its withdrawn claims are not borrowed as replication or mechanism support. Bose's own controlled results are appraised separately; no whole-sulforaphane inefficacy claim.

funding.COI: All authors declare no competing interests.

notices.limit: Current metadata and bounded exact-source query only; not a universal notice-absence guarantee.

mitotic.title: Sulforaphane, PLK1 C67 and BubR1 phosphorylation: version-bounded cellular evidence

published.title: Proteolysis-Assisted Cyclization Facilitates Site-Centric Target Deconvolution of Isothiocyanates
published.access: Complete publisher/PubMed abstract, citation and public metadata; full-text link redirected to abstract, ordinary PDF and linked supplement returned 403.

preprint.title: Proteolysis-assisted cyclization facilitates site-centric target deconvolution of isothiocyanates
preprint.relationship: Same-titled work and matching scientific author group; exact published-versus-preprint experimental identity cannot be established from the published abstract. No cross-version pooling or independent-study credit.

supplement.version: Preprint-linked SupplementaryInformationR2.pdf; not the inaccessible 2026 publisher supplement
supplement.read_scope: Title/author identity, biological figure captions 1-5 and relevant Supplementary Fig. 4 native page; synthetic procedures and spectra not fully read.

model.culture: DMEM/10% FBS for maintenance; general treatment protocol uses overnight serum-free conditioning and serum-free probe exposure.
model.normal_model_limit: Main mechanistic experiments use HEK293T; supplementary ROS caption says HEK293. These are not evidence from normal primary muscle, patient-derived MVA cells or an in vivo exposure model.

interventions.SFN: Parent sulforaphane in cellular/kinase/MTT functional experiments; supplier reported under other purchased ITCs as J&K Scientific. Specific SFN catalog, stereochemistry and purity not verified in the passages read.
interventions.SFyne: Synthesized alkyne analogue, used for direct site-adduct MS mapping; not identical to SFN and less potent in the reported MTT assay.
interventions.ITCyne: Propargyl isothiocyanate reactivity probe used after cell lysis in SFN competition/QTRP; a separate molecule.

evidence.anchor: Preprint main pp7-9; Fig.4a-b, PDF physical33-34
evidence.claim: PLK1 C67 is a candidate SFN-responsive site with orthogonal probe evidence.
evidence.details: Parent SFN 100 µM for 4 h reduced subsequent ITCyne C67 peptide labeling; representative H/L ratio 9.5. SFyne 100 µM for 4 h gave an MS/MS-assigned adduct at PLK1 C67.
evidence.n: QTRP biological duplicates; CV <40% for quantified sites; target threshold H/L >=1.5.
evidence.limit: QTRP signal is not a pure occupancy estimate because protein abundance can change; PLK1 indeed declines. Direct adduct mapping is for SFyne, not chemically unmodified parent SFN.

evidence.claim: Actual SFN 100 µM for 4 h reduces the p-BubR1 signal alongside PLK1 protein.
evidence.controls: WT and shRNA-plk1 contexts, DMSO/SFN lanes; separate total BubR1 and GAPDH bands.
evidence.phosphosite: Thr680, from anti-BubR1-phospho-T680 antibody ab200061; total BubR1 ab183496.
evidence.n: Representative immunoblot; experiment-specific biological n/densitometry/P values not supplied.
evidence.limit: A phosphorylation/substrate readout, not increased BUBR1 abundance or direct measurement of spindle-checkpoint competence, faithful segregation, allele rescue or muscle output. Total BubR1 bands are qualitatively retained, not a quantified equivalence claim.

evidence.claim: Purified-enzyme inhibition is weak relative to the cellular protein-loss finding.
evidence.details: Authors report SFN inhibition only above 200 µM; staurosporine positive control IC50 <1 µM. ADP-Glo, 50 µM ATP and 50 µM DTT, 1 h compound incubation.
evidence.limit: No numerical SFN kinase IC50, CI or panel-specific n is supplied. Do not label SFN a potent direct PLK1 kinase inhibitor at the 100 µM cell exposure.

evidence.claim: Controls support a PLK1 protein-loss mechanism involving C67 and proteasome activity.
evidence.details: PLK1 mRNA is not detectably reduced; Cyclin B1 is qualitatively preserved during the PLK1 protein titration. MG132 5 µM for 24 h before SFN 100 µM for 4 h alleviates PLK1 loss. PLK1 C67S mutation attenuates/resists protein loss across SFN 0-100 µM, 4 h.
evidence.qPCR_n: Three independent samples, each measured in triplicate, normalized to GAPDH; caption says representative triplicates.
evidence.limit: Preserved Cyclin B1 is an indirect control, not a comprehensive cell-cycle analysis. MG132/C67S support but do not establish an exclusive mechanism or complete kinetic degradation model. Figure 4 does not show mutant rescue of p-BubR1 itself.

evidence.anchor: Preprint Fig.4j and Extended Data Fig.2; MTT Methods
evidence.claim: PLK1 C67S or knockdown attenuates SFN-associated MTT loss without eliminating it.
evidence.n: Biological triplicates stated in MTT Methods; representative triplicates, SD and two-sided Student t tests in captions.
evidence.duration: MTT Methods specify 24 h compound exposure then 4 h MTT incubation. Fig.4j caption does not repeat duration; Fig.3f separately labels its screen 100 µM/4 h, a reporting inconsistency not silently reconciled.
evidence.limit: Curve labels are source-native, not newly fitted estimates; no CIs or fit model supplied. MTT is a metabolic viability proxy, not a direct death count or chromosome-function assay. Dose-wise test multiplicity is not stated. Partial resistance does not prove PLK1/BubR1 is the sole toxicity mechanism.

reporting_limits: QTRP Results say 500 µM ITCyne after lysis, whereas Methods/Fig.3 caption say 1 mM; retain discrepancy.
General 4 h compound treatment states 0.1% DMSO. MTT describes 100x DMSO stock solutions without a clear matched final vehicle statement.
Fig.3f caption gives 100 µM/4 h for its MTT screen while general MTT Methods specify 24 h; do not transplant one duration to every assay.
Supplementary Fig.4 in the linked R2 PDF contains NRF2/ROS; the main's library paragraph refers to Supplementary Fig.4 for reproducibility, while the linked PDF labels reproducibility Fig.5.
Supplementary Fig.4b-c says HEK293 whereas its blot panel and main use HEK293T; ROS dose/time, gating, test and referenced Methods are not fully specified in the passages available.
Fig.4i caption says C67S abolished PLK1 loss, while Results say attenuated. Conservative interpretation is attenuation/resistance rather than complete protection.
Quantitative biological n and densitometric inference for Fig.4 blots, randomization/blinding and raw full blots were not established in this bounded review.

supplement_context.observation: Native blot displays SFN 0/25/50/100 µM, NRF2/KEAP1/PLK1/GAPDH and described biphasic NRF2 behavior; ROS plots include vehicle/SFN/arsenite/positive-control groups with three dots each.
supplement_context.limit: Selected auxiliary context only. Missing dose/time and analysis details for ROS prevent a mechanistic rescue or safety inference; these panels do not establish normal-cell safety.

interpretation.supported: A high-concentration preprint cell experiment supports SFN-associated PLK1 protein loss with lower BubR1 Thr680 phosphorylation and a C67-linked contribution to MTT loss.
not_supported: PLK1 as the sole SFN target
Published 2026 confirmation of this exact figure
interpretation.MVA_relevance: Mechanistic caution and assay-design context only. Do not infer clinical harm, food effects or disease rescue from this transformed-cell exposure.

funding.source: Preprint acknowledgments list Chinese national research/natural-science grants, Beijing National Laboratory support and XPLORER PRIZE.
funding.COI: Preprint and public published record declare no competing interests.
funding.limit: Funding declarations are retained; absence of undisclosed interests is not established.

notices.limit: Current retained metadata and two exact-source queries only; no universal notice absence or exhaustive version history. Research Square landing page was inaccessible; v1 is the retrieved public version, not a proved latest version.

reading.relevant_preprint_main_sections: Site-centric SFN target mapping and PLK1 Results; selected Discussion framing; relevant compound/culture/antibody/plasmid/knockdown/MTT/kinase/qPCR/Western Methods and funding/COI.

citation.authors: Wang M, Pu D, Zhao Y, Chen J, Zhu S, Lu A, Liao Z, Sun Y, Xiao Q

diabetic.conclusion: Retain the authors-reported actual-sulforaphane grip-strength positive in spontaneous type 2 diabetic db/db mice, separately from muscle/lean-mass and pathway findings. Preparation-specific dosing, statistical robustness and transfer remain unresolved at original-abstract depth.

secondary_pointer_not_adopted.status: UNVERIFIED_PRIMARY; supplied secondary pointer and exposed secondary search snippet only. No primary-method confirmation.

identity_boundaries: Do not inherit explicit D,L identity from separate oral muscle/aging studies.

Do not equate with L-SULFORAPHANE CHEMBL1627201, unspecified SULFORAPHANE CHEMBL48802, its R/(-) aliases, glucoraphanin, broccoli foods, extracts or commercial supplements on parent-name matching alone.

design.model_as_reported: Spontaneous type 2 diabetic db/db mice and db/m littermate comparison wording
design.arms_as_reported: The abstract states db/m and littermate db/db mice were treated with SFN or DMSO. Exact group allocation and factorial contrast are not supplied.
design.control: DMSO vehicle named; db/m model comparator named
design.sex: Male is indexed in PubMed MeSH; not independently established from primary Methods

outcomes.finding: Authors report a statistically significant increase.
outcomes.test_or_contrast: Named vehicle control exists in Methods wording, but exact statistical contrast/test/interaction not supplied.
outcomes.normalization: UNKNOWN whether absolute force, body-mass-normalized or another scaling; number of pulls, limb configuration and aggregation unknown
outcomes.limits: Not isolated-muscle evoked force, endurance or a verified lean-mass-independent effect.

outcomes.finding: Authors report increases in db/db mice after SFN.
outcomes.statistical_significance: The abstract explicitly says significant for grip; it does not provide mass-endpoint P values or tests.
outcomes.limits: Not body-weight change, muscle-specific force, or necessarily mass-independent functional rescue. Absolute versus relative normalization unknown.

outcomes.finding: Authors report restored organization after SFN.
outcomes.limits: No quantified native morphometry, denominator or independent structural analysis available.

outcomes.endpoint: Nrf2/HO-1 and inflammatory/apoptotic proteins; oxidative/inflammatory transcripts
outcomes.finding: Authors report pathway activation, lower inflammatory/apoptotic protein expression and regulated oxidative/inflammatory transcripts.
outcomes.limits: Not a genetic Nrf2 perturbation or proof of Nrf2 necessity. No genetic intervention is described in the abstract; full-paper mechanistic design remains unverified.

nulls_and_harms.null_outcomes: No explicit null outcomes given in the accessible original abstract; do not infer the full paper contains none.
nulls_and_harms.db_m_treatment_effect: Not described quantitatively; no normal-control sparing/safety claim.
nulls_and_harms.harms_or_deaths: Not reported in the examined abstract; not evidence of absence or safety.

transfer_limits: No BUBR1 abundance, localization, chromosome fidelity or actual-BUB1B-allele rescue established.
No MVA or human efficacy evidence from this model.
No human dose conversion or formulation equivalence.
Do not borrow Nrf2 knockout-dependence or functional outcomes from the separate aging, mdx or mitotic studies.
Main-access failure does not negate the reported functional positive or produce a negative efficacy result.

publication_status.status: No exact-paper notice identified in the retained bounded PubMed, Europe PMC, Crossref and exact-source search checks. This is not a universal notice-absence guarantee.

review.independent_review_depth: Accepted independent review of complete retained main narrative and five captions, plus original notices and identity relations. Native pixels, supplement, raw observations and primer table were not independently read.

review.scope: Source-specific scope retained in the bound review and reading-scope artifacts.
review.independent_review_depth: Accepted independent review of complete retained scientific main narrative, six captions and table narratives/footnotes. Native pixels, supplement, raw data and all numerical transcript-table cells were not independently read.

review.scope: Root independent verification of central Fig4 experiment only, not full source re-audit

review.independent_review_depth: Root CORE_CLAIMS_PASS covers complete qualification plus selected preprint passages and native Figure 4 physical page 33. The remaining preprint, published main, all supplement/Extended Data panels and raw fits were not independently reviewed.

review.scope: Source-specific scope retained in the bound review and reading-scope artifacts.
review.independent_review_depth: Root accepted the complete qualification and live original PubMed abstract/identity fields at original-abstract depth. Primary main, Methods, native outcomes, supplement and raw data remain unread; access metadata was not independently re-retrieved.

synthesis_scope.source_local_followup_status: The original muscle packet listed aging and diabetic studies as then-unread follow-ups. Their later separate accepted qualifications supersede those historical pointer statuses only in this synthesis. The glucoraphanin-rich broccoli pointer is outside this proposal.
synthesis_scope.review_depth: Muscle and aging retain their independent accepted text/caption scopes; diabetic retains root acceptance at original-abstract depth; mitotic retains root CORE_CLAIMS_PASS for the central experiment, not an independent full-source review.
synthesis_scope.raw_payload_policy: Portable scientific qualification only. Original mains, notices, figures, XML and access witnesses remain outside Git, bound by external packet manifests.

cross_source_limits: No pooling of preparation-specific doses, effects, denominators or cohorts.
No inference that distinct papers or within-paper repeats provide independently replicated BUBR1, muscle or MVA rescue.
Withdrawals remove support; they do not establish sulforaphane inefficacy. Oral nulls and diabetic access failure are not whole-compound negative verdicts.
No Nrf2 genetic-dependency result is borrowed from cited literature, and the PLK1 C67S construct is not a BUB1B patient allele.
No human-dose conversion, tissue-exposure bridge, food/precursor/retail equivalence or clinical safety-margin inference.
Useful function, renewal and chromosome fidelity remain separate criteria; no study here demonstrates the actual BUB1B-allele disease correction or superiority over niacin/apitegromab.
